analysis:
Docs-only PR: docs/reference/configuration.md (the real change is at head lines 393-395) and a new measurement report docs/reports/2026-10-21-mixed-step-prefill-geometry.md. No code, protocol, key-handling, attestation, or authorization behavior changes. The units show the new rows for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS, and the solo-prefill stripe row (line 395) is expanded.

Security-relevant observations:
- The new knobs are env-var tuning of prefill chunk size and step budget. They are described as forwarded to the LaunchAgent, so they come from the operator's own environment. The operator is already an adversary (ADV-001) who controls the provider process, and a malformed value falls back to defaults. The knobs do not touch the E2E encryption path (T-008), attestation or App Attest authorization (TB-011), or the coordinator trust boundary, so they add no new attack surface.
- The report notes that Gemma 4's wide geometry raises activation memory. GPT-OSS and dense Qwen keep 512/2048 by default, and the opt-in can push peaks 0.1-0.5 GiB past the reserve into the OS reserve. This is an availability and memory-admission consideration (resource exhaustion, a DoS-class concern) for a self-opted-in operator on their own machine. It is documented, not a regression. Coordinator memory admission is platform-owned, so I could not verify it.
- The report states that no load arm used repeated prefixes. Chunk size changes the recurrent-checkpoint grid (every 2048 tokens under the opt-in) for dense Qwen. This could marginally alter the prefix-cache hit and miss pattern relevant to T-041's TTFT oracle, but the caches remain account-scoped, HMAC-keyed and TTL-bound, and nothing in the evidence shows a changed trust property. This is an unverified integration question, not a finding.
- Code behavior (the Gemma 4 default of 2048/4096, the media ceiling of 512, the raise to 1120) is claimed only in the docs. The implementing source is not supplied, so the documented claims are unverified against the code.

No findings.
